sentences.en: If you are not familiar with these bonus episodes, we've been doing it for perhaps the last year or so, and these are kind of more bite-sized episodes
sentences.zh: 如果你对这些番外节目还不熟悉的话，过去一年左右我们一直在做这个，这些都是比较短小精悍的节目，

sentences.en: where we take a popular psychology term, a phrase, a concept, a theory, and we break it down for you and we reveal what it really means, what it's actually about.
sentences.zh: 我们会挑选一个大众心理学词汇、短语、概念或理论，为你进行剖析，揭示它的真实含义和它真正的本质。

sentences.en: Basically, we myth-bust some common psychological ideas that you probably see online that maybe have lost their original meaning,
sentences.zh: 基本上，我们要打破一些常见的心理学迷思，这些迷思你可能经常在网上看到，而且它们可能已经失去了原本的含义，

sentences.en: but we also get into the deeper history of these terms, how they came to be so popular, and also some fun, you know, also less than fun facts that come along with them.
sentences.zh: 但我们也会深入探讨这些术语的深层历史、它们是如何变得如此受欢迎的，以及一些有趣但有时也不那么好笑的冷知识。

sentences.en: Today, we have a very interesting one.
sentences.zh: 今天我们要聊一个非常有趣的话题。

sentences.en: I do want to give you a heads up though.
sentences.zh: 不过我得先提醒大家一下。

sentences.en: This episode does include some details about violence and domestic violence.
sentences.zh: 本期节目确实包含一些关于暴力和家庭暴力的细节。

sentences.en: So if that's something that you aren't particularly interested in hearing about or you're sensitive to, I would probably skip this one.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你对这类话题不是很感兴趣，或者比较敏感，建议你最好跳过这一集。

sentences.en: It's not too much detail, but we definitely mention it.
sentences.zh: 细节不是很多，但我们确实提到了。

sentences.en: We are talking about Stockholm Syndrome.
sentences.zh: 我们要谈的是斯德哥尔摩综合征。

sentences.en: I think these days when we use the term Stockholm Syndrome, it's often quite colloquial and quite casually, normally in reference to a situation
sentences.zh: 我想现在当我们使用“斯德哥尔摩综合征”这个词时，往往是非常通俗和随意的，通常是指这样一种情况：

sentences.en: where someone has kind of fallen in love or become very loyal to someone or something that they shouldn't be loyal to or which is harming them.
sentences.zh: 某人对一个本不该效忠或正在伤害自己的人或事物产生了爱意，或者变得非常忠诚。

sentences.en: Normally, in regards to love, there is a very famous One Direction song of the same name where they basically just sing about being intoxicated by this girl,
sentences.zh: 通常在爱情方面，有一个同名的非常著名的单曲，是One Direction唱的，他们基本上就是在歌唱被这个女孩迷得神魂颠倒，

sentences.en: you know, they're obsessed with her, they long for her, they've got Stockholm Syndrome.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们对她痴迷，渴望她，他们患上了斯德哥尔摩综合征。

sentences.en: It is so much more than that.
sentences.zh: 但实际情况要复杂得多。

sentences.en: And it's a lot more serious than that as well.
sentences.zh: 而且要严肃得多。

sentences.en: It's not about obsession.
sentences.zh: 这与痴迷无关。

sentences.en: It's not about intoxication.
sentences.zh: 这与神魂颠倒无关。

sentences.en: It's actually very much about survival.
sentences.zh: 这其实很大程度上关乎生存。

sentences.en: So Stockholm Syndrome, in a psychological sense, in a forensic sense, is a term used to describe what we would call a paradoxical emotional bond that forms between a victim
sentences.zh: 因此，斯德哥尔摩综合征在心理学意义上、在法医心理学意义上，是一个用来描述受害者与威胁、伤害、控制或囚禁他们的人之间，

sentences.en: and someone who is threatening, harming, controlling, or holding them captive.
sentences.zh: 形成的一种我们称之为“矛盾的情感纽带”的术语。

sentences.en: That might include having positive feelings towards a captor or an abuser, having sympathy for their perspective, feeling gratitude for small acts of kindness
sentences.zh: 这可能包括对绑架者或虐待者产生积极的情感，同情他们的视角，在可能充满不友善、恐惧和不信任的整体残酷大背景下，

sentences.en: against maybe a broader backdrop of unkindness, fear and distrust of people who are trying to intervene and get you away from this person.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为一些小小的善举而心怀感激，并且对那些试图介入并将你从这个人身边解救出来的人感到恐惧和不信任。

sentences.en: Basically, any feeling or reaction that we kind of see as being irrational or counterintuitive towards somebody who means you harm, is causing you harm,
sentences.zh: 基本上，任何对一个对你心怀恶意、正在对你造成伤害的人所产生的不合理或违反直觉的情感或反应，

sentences.en: and yet people feel a sense of loyalty to them or a sense of an emotional bond to them for strange reasons, but also less than strange reasons, as we'll get into.
sentences.zh: 而人们却出于种种奇怪的原因（当然也有不那么奇怪的原因，我们稍后会讨论）对他们产生忠诚感或情感纽带。

sentences.en: From the outside, the reason why we call it a paradoxical emotional bond is because, as I said,
sentences.zh: 从外部来看，我们之所以称之为矛盾的情感纽带，是因为正如我所说，

sentences.en: you know, it kind of goes against how we think people should react in situations like this.
sentences.zh: 这违背了我们认为人们在面对这种情境时应该做出的反应。

sentences.en: We have this idea that if somebody is hurting you, you wouldn't want to be around that person.
sentences.zh: 我们有一种观念：如果有人在伤害你，你绝不想和这个人待在一起。

sentences.en: If somebody is holding you captive, you're not going to have positive feelings towards them because they've taken away your agency and your independence
sentences.zh: 如果有人将你囚禁，你绝不会对他们产生正面的感觉，因为他们剥夺了你的自主权、独立性、

sentences.en: and your privacy and your freedom, so shouldn't you have bad feelings about that person?
sentences.zh: 隐私和自由，所以你难道不应该对这个人怀恨在心吗？

sentences.en: Shouldn't you hate that person?
sentences.zh: 难道你不是应该恨这个人吗？

sentences.en: And most importantly, shouldn't you want to escape that person?
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，难道你不想从这个人身边逃跑吗？

sentences.en: Shouldn't you want to take any opportunity offered to you to get away from them?
sentences.zh: 难道你不想抓住提供给你的任何机会离开他们吗？

sentences.en: The thing is, this isn't always the case.
sentences.zh: 问题是，事实并非总是如此。

sentences.en: And it's not that these people are choosing or siding with an abuser or a person who holds power over them.
sentences.zh: 并不是说这些人主动选择站在施虐者或掌控他们权力的人一边。

sentences.en: Stockholm Syndrome is a survival strategy that forms under conditions where a person has so little choice and is experiencing such an extreme situation,
sentences.zh: 斯德哥尔摩综合征是一种生存策略，它形成于一个人几乎别无选择、经历着极端境况的条件下，

sentences.en: a once-in-a-lifetime kind of stress, that they act in the only way they see is available to them to survive.
sentences.zh: 这是一种千载难逢的巨大压力，以至于他们只能采取自己认为唯一可行的办法来存活下去。

sentences.en: And in that situation, the way they do that is by forming an emotional bond, by perhaps having sympathy, seeing their captor or their abuser as human as a way to connect with them.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，他们这样做的途径就是建立情感纽带，也许是通过产生同情，把绑架者或虐待者看作是有血有肉的人，以此来与他们建立连接。

sentences.en: So the term first came from a very real hostage situation in Sweden in 1973.
sentences.zh: 这个词最初源于1973年瑞典发生的一起真实的绑架人质事件。

sentences.en: It was a bank robbery at a credit bank in Stockholm and it involved two captors and four employees and they were held hostage for six days.
sentences.zh: 这是斯德哥尔摩一家信贷银行发生的银行抢劫案，涉及两名绑架者和四名人质，他们被劫持了六天。

sentences.en: Now, what made the case so famous was not the robbery, although that definitely made headlines.
sentences.zh: 然而，让这个案件如此出名的并不是抢劫本身，尽管那确实登上了各大头条。

sentences.en: It was what happened afterwards.
sentences.zh: 而是事后发生的事情。

sentences.en: Some of the captives, you know, as they were being rescued, almost seemed to fear the police more than the men who were holding them hostage.
sentences.zh: 一些人质在获救时，似乎对警察的恐惧甚至超过了劫持他们的人。

sentences.en: They seemed to have sympathy for these men.
sentences.zh: 他们似乎对这些劫匪充满了同情。

sentences.en: There was one hostage in particular, her name was Kristen Enmark, who essentially
sentences.zh: 其中有一名人质叫克里斯滕·恩马克，基本上可以说她

sentences.en: very much felt sorry for her captors, very much criticized aspects of the police response, even went on to raise money for the legal defenses of her captors and their captors
sentences.zh: 非常同情绑架者，极力批评警方的应对方式，甚至还为绑架者筹集法律辩护资金，而她的绑架者则拒绝作证，并表示完全信任他们。

sentences.en: refused to testify, said they trusted them fully.
sentences.zh: 这种令人困惑的反应引起了精神病学家和法医心理学家的极大关注，他们认为这种反应方式相当反直觉，

sentences.en: And this confusing reaction really caught the attention of psychiatrists and forensic psychologists who were seeing this way of responding as pretty counterintuitive,
sentences.zh: 但同时也非常有趣。

sentences.en: but also very interesting.
sentences.zh: 他们想知道在那场危机中究竟发生了什么，那家银行里到底发生了什么，才让这些人这么快就变成了那些伤害并囚禁他们的人的“同盟”。

sentences.en: They wanted to know kind of what happened in that situation, what happened in that bank that had turned these people so quickly into seemingly allies of the people
sentences.zh: 这就是他们创造“斯德哥尔摩综合征”这个词来指代这四个人的原因。

sentences.en: who were harming them and holding them captive.
sentences.zh: 他们将这种现象视为一种近乎医学上的状况或医学反应，即他们对这一事件做出的心理反应。

sentences.en: And that's where they got the term Stockholm Syndrome to refer to these four people.
sentences.zh: 这只是这个故事的一个非常简化的版本。

sentences.en: And what they saw as kind of like almost a medical condition or a medical reaction, a psychological reaction they had to this event.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们可以花上两个小时，逐分逐秒地分析当时发生的事情，深入探讨结局以及事后的发展。

sentences.en: This is a very simplified telling of the story.
sentences.zh: 但这是这段经历第一次拥有了一个名字。

sentences.en: You know, we could spend two hours going moment by moment about what happened and diving more into the outcomes and what happened afterwards.
sentences.zh: 另一个著名的案件是帕蒂·赫斯特案。

sentences.en: But it was the first time that this experience had a name.
sentences.zh: 你可能听说过这个。

sentences.en: Another famous case is that of Patty HearSt.
sentences.zh: 赫斯特是一名19岁的

sentences.en: You may have heard about this.
sentences.zh: 美国女演员。

sentences.en: Hearst was a 19-year-old
sentences.zh: 她是当时一位非常著名的报业大亨和政治家的孙女。

sentences.en: American actress.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫

sentences.en: She was the granddaughter of a very famous newspaper publisher and politician at the time.
sentences.zh: 威廉·伦道夫·赫斯特。

sentences.en: His name was
sentences.zh: 1974年，她在自己的公寓里被一个名为“共生解放军”的组织绑架。

sentences.en: William Randolph HearSt.
sentences.zh: 那是一个激进的政治组织，在她被囚禁期间，出现了一些视频和录音，显示她在批评自己的家庭、甚至与家庭断绝关系。

sentences.en: She was kidnapped from her apartment in 1974 by like a Liberation Army group.
sentences.zh: 她甚至改名为塔尼亚。

sentences.en: They were a radical political group and during her captivity these videos came out, these recordings came out of her criticizing her family, rejecting her family.
sentences.zh: 人们看到她与该组织成员一起参与了一场银行抢劫，在抢劫过程中她本有机会逃跑，但她没有。

sentences.en: She even adopted the name Tanya.
sentences.zh: 后来她被捕了。

sentences.en: She was seen taking part in a bank robbery with members of the group where she herself would have had an opportunity to escape and she was arrested.
sentences.zh: 她不是被营救的，而是被逮捕并因协助他们犯罪而接受审判，她的辩护律师辩称她患有一种罕见的情况。

sentences.en: She was not rescued, she was arrested and put on trial for assisting them in crimes and her defense argued that she had this rare thing.
sentences.zh: 她患有斯德哥尔摩综合征，她被胁迫了，她饱受囚禁带来的深重心理创伤，然而陪审团在看过证据后说：

sentences.en: She had Stockholm Syndrome, she'd been coerced, she'd been deeply psychologically affected by captivity and the jury saw the evidence and said
sentences.zh: “不，我们依然要判你有罪。”

sentences.en: no, we're still going to convict you.
sentences.zh: 所以他们当时并不相信这一点，但现在我想我们的看法肯定有所不同了。

sentences.en: So they didn't believe it but now I think we definitely see it a little bit differently.
sentences.zh: 我们看到的是一个非常年轻的女孩，身处一个让她感到不安全的极端压力环境中。

sentences.en: We see what was a very young girl in a very stressful situation where she didn't feel safe.
sentences.zh: 她唯一能信任的人就是这些对她心怀不轨的人，但他们又是她身边仅有的人，于是她几乎和他们陷入了一种畸形的关系中。

sentences.en: The only people she could trust were these people who essentially meant her harm but they were the only ones there and she kind of fell into a relationship almost with them.
sentences.zh: 所以，我一直没有把这称为心理健康诊断，不知道你们有没有注意到这一点，这是有原因的，因为它根本不是。

sentences.en: So I've kind of been not referring to this as a mental health diagnosis, I don't know if you've noticed that but for a reason because it isn't.
sentences.zh: 它至今仍未被接受为——

sentences.en: It still isn't accepted as
sentences.zh: 我想它依然没有被医学界接受为一个医疗诊断。

sentences.en: I guess it still isn't accepted as yeah, just as a medical diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 它没有被收录在《精神疾病诊断与统计手册》（DSM）中。

sentences.en: It isn't included in the DSM.
sentences.zh: 也没有普遍认可的诊断标准。

sentences.en: There are no universally agreed upon diagnostic criteria.
sentences.zh: 斯德哥尔摩综合征主要只是一个描述性标签，因为它也极其罕见。

sentences.en: Stockholm Syndrome is mainly just a descriptive label because it's also incredibly rare.
sentences.zh: 首先，你知道的，人们被长期扣为人质并活着逃出来的情况极其罕见，而在这种情况下，根据

sentences.en: Firstly, you know, it's incredibly rare for people to be held hostage for extended periods of time and to make it out alive and in those situations only about
sentences.zh: 联邦调查局（FBI）的分析，

sentences.en: 8% of people according to
sentences.zh: 只有大约

sentences.en: FBI analysis
sentences.zh: 8%的人

sentences.en: exhibit what we would call Stockholm
sentences.zh: 表现出我们所说的斯德哥尔摩

sentences.en: Syndrome.
sentences.zh: 综合征。

sentences.en: So of, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以在他们研究过的

sentences.en: 1,200 hostage situations that they looked at of those that had a surviving person,
sentences.zh: 1200起人质事件中，在那些有人幸存的案例里，
只有8%的

sentences.en: 8% of people were kind of experiencing even just a level of sympathy, loyalty, care, trust for their captors.
sentences.zh: 人，也就是说仅有8%的人对绑架者表现出某种程度的同情、忠诚、关心或信任。

sentences.en: There's another often discussed case in relation to Stockholm
sentences.zh: 还有一个与斯德哥尔摩

sentences.en: Syndrome.
sentences.zh: 综合征相关的常被讨论的案件。

sentences.en: This woman called Natasha
sentences.zh: 这个女性名叫娜塔莎

sentences.en: Kampuschke.
sentences.zh: 坎普许。

sentences.en: She was kidnapped in Austria.
sentences.zh: 她在奥地利被绑架。

sentences.en: She was 10.
sentences.zh: 当时她10岁。
